1.POST PARTUM HAEMORRHAGE; PPH

P0 PPH

Bleeding >500ml within 24 hours of normal delivery and >1000ml after CS

Minor PPH: 500 – 1000ml

Major PPH

Moderate 1000 – 2000

Severe >2000ml

Secondary PPH: from 24 hours of delivery to 12 weeks postpartum.

Most common cause of obstetric haemorrhage

Identify risk factor antenatally and I/P

Correction of anemia morbidity after PPH

Shock index = HR/ systolic BP => early marker of haemodynamic compromise

Oxytocin

SVD 10units, I/M

CS 5 units I/V, no more units are beneficial.

Uterine – massage routinely – no role in prophylaxis.

Tranexamic acid; 500 – 1000mg (in C/S in women @ risk of PPH)

Ergometrine + oxytocin without HTN reduces minor haemorrhage (Given in patient with risk of haemorrhage)

oxytocin => routine use

Ergometrine, Tranexamic acid => in women with risk factor.
